title: Microsoft Purview Data Security Investigations: Admin and Contributor roles added to existing Purview role groups
summary: The briefing's role assignments, automatic access, membership controls and consumption billing are supported by Microsoft documentation and the roadmap. Microsoft gives differing navigation and permission guidance for the dedicated administrator group, which should be noted. The statement that the change adds no automated action goes beyond the published description.

claims.claim: Security Administrator inherits Microsoft Entra Security Administrator membership, conferring its DSI Contributor access.
claims.quote: the Security Administrator role from Microsoft Entra ID is assigned to this role group. Therefore, this role group inherits the capabilities and membership of the Security Administrator role from Microsoft Entra ID.

claims.claim: Role group permission changes can take up to 30 minutes to apply.
claims.quote: After you configure your role groups, it might take up to 30 minutes for the role group permissions to apply to assigned users across your organization.

claims.claim: The role change adds no automated action.
claims.quote: Searched: Data Security Investigations role automatically simplification. Read DSI overview, permissions, billing and Get started search excerpts. They describe role additions and existing automated processing, but do not explicitly establish that this change adds no automated action.
claims.fix: Replace 'No change: the roles grant access to existing DSI functions and add no automated action.' with 'The roadmap describes this change as adding DSI roles to existing Purview role groups.'

claims.where: front matter: licensing.model; licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: DSI has consumption billing based on stored data and computing capacity for AI analysis.
claims.quote: Billing in Data Security Investigations is based solely on the combination of the amount of stored data and the associated computing capacity needed for AI analysis.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: DSI billing is not based on a dedicated enterprise plan or licence.
claims.quote: It isn't based on a dedicated enterprise plan or license.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: Microsoft has published no licence or charge specific to this role change.
claims.quote: Searched: Data Security Investigations role-based access simplification licence price charge role change. Opened DSI billing, overview and permissions; read Get started search excerpts. These document storage and compute billing, not a licence or charge for adding these roles.

claims.claim: The storage meter charges per gigabyte per month for stored investigation data.
claims.quote: You pay for storage on a gigabyte (GB) per month basis for stored data associated with all investigations in your organization.

claims.where: Cost and licensing: Meters; licensing.notes; rationale: cost
claims.claim: AI analysis uses Data Security Investigations Compute Units, billed for the units consumed.
claims.quote: Data Security Investigations Compute Units (compute unit) measure the computational capacity needed to run the AI analysis within Data Security Investigations. ... You pay only for the compute units you use.

claims.claim: Setting up DSI billing requires an Azure subscription in the same tenant.
claims.quote: Before you can use Data Security Investigations in your organization, you must configure both billing models. ... An Azure subscription in the same tenant as Microsoft Purview.

claims.claim: The storage meter bills through an Azure subscription linked during setup.
claims.quote: Storage meter billing requires a link to an Azure subscription for pay-as-you-go billing.

claims.claim: Microsoft directs readers to the Azure Microsoft Purview pricing page for storage rates.
claims.quote: For more data storage rates and pricing, see Data Security Investigations storage meter pricing.

claims.claim: Microsoft recommends Azure budgets and spending alerts for the DSI resource group and meter.
claims.quote: Create budgets for the Data Security Investigations resource group and meter level. ... Configure alerts when spending approaches defined thresholds

claims.where: Why it matters; Cost and licensing: Spend controls and Indirect cost
claims.claim: Only Admin-role holders can open the Pay-as-you-go usage dashboard, including the newly entitled broad-group members.
claims.quote: Only users assigned the Data Security Investigations Admin role can access the Pay-as-you-go usage dashboard.

claims.claim: Azure budgets and alerts are not caps that stop consumption.
claims.quote: Notifications are triggered when the budget thresholds are exceeded. Resources aren't affected, and your consumption isn't stopped.

claims.claim: The usage dashboard tracks storage and compute use rather than setting a spending cap.
claims.quote: Use the Pay-as-you-go usage dashboard to quickly view and track data storage and compute unit usage for each investigation in your organization.

claims.claim: Deleting an investigation stops charges for its associated data storage.
claims.quote: When you delete an investigation, you stop paying for the associated data storage amount.

claims.claim: Investigation storage charges are prorated by the number of days stored.
claims.quote: The charges are prorated to the number of days the data was stored in the billing cycle.

claims.where: controls[0].ui; Governance controls table; Governance guidance
claims.claim: Purview removal path is Settings > Roles and scopes > Role groups > Role groups for Microsoft Purview solutions > role group > Edit > Edit members of the role group > Remove members.
claims.quote: Go to Settings > Roles and scopes ... Select Role groups. ... On Role groups for Microsoft Purview solutions, select a Microsoft Purview role group ... Select Edit ... On Edit members of the role group ... Select Remove members

claims.where: controls[0].api; Governance controls table; Governance guidance
claims.claim: Remove-RoleGroupMember -Identity "<role-group>" -Member "<user-UPN>" removes a member from the selected role group.
claims.quote: Use the Remove-RoleGroupMember cmdlet to remove a member of a management role group. ... The Identity parameter specifies the role group ... The Member parameter specifies who to remove ... User ID or user principal name (UPN)

claims.claim: The DSI page gives Settings > Roles and groups > Role groups > Data Security Investigations Admins > Edit > Choose users.
claims.quote: Select Settings ... select Roles and groups, then select Role groups ... Select the Data Security Investigations Admins role group, then select Edit. ... Select Choose users
claims.fix: Keep the cited path, and add to controls[1].note: 'The DSI permissions page calls this navigation Roles and groups; the general Purview permissions page calls it Roles and scopes.' Both pages are already cited.

claims.claim: Add-RoleGroupMember -Identity "<role-group>" -Member "<user-UPN>" adds a user to the dedicated administrator role group.
claims.quote: Use the Add-RoleGroupMember cmdlet to add members to a management role group. ... The Identity parameter specifies the role group to add a member to. ... User ID or user principal name (UPN)

claims.claim: Purview addition path is Settings > Roles and scopes > Role groups > Role groups for Microsoft Purview solutions > role group > Edit > Edit members of the role group > Choose users.
claims.quote: Go to Settings > Roles and scopes ... Select Role groups. ... On Role groups for Microsoft Purview solutions, select a Microsoft Purview role group ... Select Edit ... On Edit members of the role group, select Choose users or Choose groups.

claims.claim: Add-RoleGroupMember -Identity "<role-group>" -Member "<user-UPN>" adds membership, without claiming to set expiry.
claims.quote: Add-RoleGroupMember [-Identity] <RoleGroupIdParameter> -Member <SecurityPrincipalIdParameter> ... When you add a member to a role group, the member is given the effective permissions provided by the management roles assigned to the role group.

claims.claim: The general Purview portal membership procedures require an account assigned the Role management role.
claims.quote: Sign in to the Microsoft Purview portal by using credentials for an admin account assigned the Role management role.
claims.fix: Add to controls[1].note: 'The DSI permissions page additionally says users following its role-group configuration steps must be assigned to Data Security Investigations Admins.' The source is https://learn.microsoft.com/purview/data-security-investigations-permissions, which says 'To continue with these configuration steps ... you must be assigned to the Data Security Investigations Admins role group.'

claims.claim: Microsoft advises keeping at least one user in Data Security Investigations Admins.
claims.quote: Always have at least one user in the Data Security Investigations Admins role group so that your Data Security Investigations configuration doesn't get in to a 'zero administrator' scenario if specific users leave your organization.

claims.where: controls[2].note; Governance controls table; Governance guidance
claims.claim: After adding users on Edit members of the role group, select those users and Edit expiration to set temporary access.
claims.quote: If the selected users or groups need temporary access, select the users or groups and select Edit expiration.

claims.claim: The Add-RoleGroupMember syntax lists no expiration parameter.
claims.quote: Searched: Add-RoleGroupMember Security Compliance PowerShell expiration parameter role membership expiry. Opened Add-RoleGroupMember and read its full syntax and parameters; search excerpts repeat the same syntax, which contains no expiration parameter.

claims.claim: Removing membership also removes access to other features supplied solely by that role group.
claims.quote: When you remove a member from a role group, that member can no longer manage the features made available by the role group if the role group is the only means by which the member is granted access to the feature.

claims.claim: The broad role groups carrying DSI roles also supply permissions for other Purview solutions.
claims.quote: A role group is a set of roles that enable users to do their jobs across compliance and governance solutions in the Microsoft Purview portal.

claims.claim: Get-RoleGroupMember -Identity <role group> retrieves the selected group's current members.
claims.quote: Use the Get-RoleGroupMember cmdlet to retrieve a list of members of a management role group. ... The Identity parameter specifies the role group for which member information should be retrieved.
